questions.stem: A client with an unpaid hospital balance requests a copy of the designated medical record set. Which response is most accurate under HIPAA?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The hospital may deny access until the balance is paid because financial obligations take priority over the patient's access rights to protected health information.","B":"The entity may postpone access until the outstanding balance is resolved because account status can be addressed before the HIPAA access deadline begins.","C":"With limited exceptions, the client has a right to access these records and the request must be handled within HIPAA timelines despite the unpaid account balance.","D":"The client may inspect the designated record set but is not entitled to receive a copy unless a clinician determines that providing one is medically necessary."}}
questions.rationale: HIPAA gives individuals a broad right of access to protected health information in a designated record set, subject to limited exceptions. A covered entity may not condition this access right on payment of an unrelated medical bill, and requests must be handled within applicable HIPAA timelines.
questions.source_name: HHS — Individuals' Right of Access under HIPAA
questions.source_detail: HIPAA provides a broad right to inspect or obtain copies of PHI in a designated record set, subject to limited exceptions and response-time requirements.

questions.stem: A competent client says that cultural and religious beliefs make family participation important in end-of-life decisions. What is the nurse's best approach?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Ask the client how family members should be involved, clarify the client's preferences, and incorporate those preferences into care when clinically and legally feasible.","B":"Assume the family should make decisions because clients from cultures that value collective decision-making generally prefer to transfer personal authority to relatives.","C":"Exclude the family from discussions because patient autonomy requires individual decision-making and does not permit culturally preferred family participation.","D":"Ask the oldest family member to decide how information should be shared because age-based hierarchy is the safest way to avoid stereotyping the client's preferences."}}
questions.rationale: Culturally responsive care centers the individual patient's values and preferences rather than stereotypes. The nurse should ask how the client wants family involved and incorporate those preferences when clinically and legally feasible.
questions.source_name: HHS Office of Minority Health — National CLAS Standards
questions.source_detail: CLAS standards call for respectful, understandable care responsive to cultural health beliefs, practices, languages, and individual communication needs.

questions.stem: A client with limited English proficiency needs informed consent for a nonemergent procedure. The client's 15-year-old child offers to interpret. What is the best nursing action?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use the child if both client and child agree because family preference removes the need for qualified language assistance during a high-stakes consent discussion.","B":"Have the client sign the English form first, then obtain interpretation afterward because the signature documents consent even if comprehension is established later.","C":"Ask any bilingual employee nearby to interpret because conversational fluency is sufficient for complex medical consent even without interpreter qualification.","D":"Arrange qualified language assistance and avoid using the minor child for this nonemergent consent discussion so the client can understand and participate fully."}}
questions.rationale: HHS CLAS standards call for competent language assistance and specifically advise avoiding untrained individuals and minors as interpreters. For nonemergent informed consent, qualified language assistance supports meaningful understanding and participation.
questions.source_name: HHS Office of Minority Health — National CLAS Standards
questions.source_detail: Language assistance should be competent and provided without charge; use of untrained individuals and minors as interpreters should be avoided and discouraged.

questions.stem: A Medicare beneficiary with a terminal illness is considering the hospice benefit and asks whether hospice means all medical treatment stops. Which explanation is most accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The hospice election ends Medicare coverage for treatment of both the terminal illness and unrelated conditions because the hospice assumes responsibility for the client's care.","B":"Hospice shifts care for the terminal illness toward comfort and symptom management; Medicare generally stops paying for curative treatment of that terminal illness.","C":"Hospice permits Medicare payment for ongoing curative treatment of the terminal illness when the hospice team also provides a separate comfort-focused plan.","D":"Hospice eligibility means disease-directed treatment must be stopped for coexisting conditions as well as the terminal illness before comfort services can begin."}}
questions.rationale: Hospice changes the focus for the terminal illness to comfort and palliative symptom management rather than cure. Under the Medicare hospice election, the beneficiary waives Medicare payment for curative treatment of the terminal illness and related conditions; this does not mean all care for unrelated conditions stops.
questions.source_detail: CMS describes hospice as holistic terminal-illness care focused on comfort/palliative symptom management rather than cure and explains the Medicare hospice election.

questions.stem: A nurse holds an active multistate license under the Nurse Licensure Compact and plans to work temporarily in another NLC jurisdiction. Which statement is accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The multistate license permits practice in compact and noncompact jurisdictions as long as the nurse's primary state of residence remains an NLC member.","B":"The nurse follows the home state's scope-of-practice rules while using the multistate privilege because the license itself was issued by the home-state board.","C":"The license allows practice in other NLC jurisdictions without separate licenses, while the nurse remains subject to the practice laws of the state where care occurs.","D":"The multistate privilege covers in-person nursing in other NLC jurisdictions, while telehealth still requires a separate single-state license in the patient's location."}}
questions.rationale: A multistate license allows nursing practice in other NLC jurisdictions without separate licenses while compact eligibility is maintained. Practice remains subject to the laws and rules of the jurisdiction where the patient is located and nursing practice occurs.
questions.source_name: Nurse Licensure Compact — Nurses & the NLC
questions.source_detail: A multistate license permits practice in other NLC states/territories without additional licenses; telehealth is included and nurses practice under the applicable remote-state authority.
